properties.statement:
FOUND 2026-08-20 while putting two real gaps to Anthony through the handshake — the tool contradicts ITSELF, in the one place a user's vocabulary is decided.

=== THE TWO TEXTS, both served by the same tool ===

The PROMPT it emits, verbatim:

    "Rewrite this design gap as one plain-language question for a non-engineer.
     No graph/systems-engineering jargon. Return only the question."

The TOOL'S OWN DESCRIPTION, verbatim:

    "Read who you are talking to (their `Contributor` description) and match that
     domain; a `plain` question is not automatically one in their vocabulary, and
     swapping vocabulary is not simplifying — a systems engineer wants `interface`
     and `verification` kept."

The description learned the lesson. The template it emits did not. An agent that follows the template strips exactly the vocabulary the reader needs, and it will do so while the description sitting beside it says not to.

=== WHY IT IS THE EXPENSIVE KIND OF CONTRADICTION ===

This is the same failure shape the revise-design skill already carries a correction for — a skill and a tool description disagreeing, where the resolution was that THE TOOL IS WHAT AN AGENT READS AT CALL TIME. Here both texts come from the same tool, so that tie-breaker does not apply, and the one an agent acts on is the WORSE one: a prompt is an instruction and a description is context, so the instruction wins.

=== WHAT IT COSTS AN ARBITRARY USER'S PROJECT ===

gap_to_prompt is the single point where a detector's vocabulary becomes a human's. A beamline scientist, a flight-test engineer, an acquisitions officer: each has a domain register, and 'no jargon' flattens all of them toward the same non-engineer default. The result is a question that is easy to read and impossible to answer precisely, put to the one person who could have answered it precisely. The standing correction on file is that a persona is a VOCABULARY SWAP, not a difficulty dial — and this template is a difficulty dial.

=== EVIDENCE IT MATTERS, from the same session ===

Both gaps were answered against the description rather than the template — SE register kept, reflow2-internal jargon dropped. The resulting questions name the decomposition spine and the hosted tier, which is what makes them answerable in one word. The template's version would have said neither.

=== A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING IN THE SAME RUN, and it is a CREDIT ===

Reusing a prompt id from a previous gap's round returned `rephrase_degraded: true` and fell back to the raw detector text rather than silently accepting a mismatched answer. It said it had degraded. That is exactly the behaviour Proposal 2 wants generalised, already working here.

=== NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY ===

Changing that template changes what every gap question sounds like on every project reflow2 is used on. That is Anthony's call, not a silent edit.
